01 / SHIPPING LAB

End-of-disruption figures and how to read the mechanism

WHAT THE ANIMATION IS SAYING

Delay a ship. Draw on stock. Keep daily life supplied.

1 / Ships slow down

Fewer cargoes pass the route, while everyday demand continues.

2 / Stock buys time

The tank supplies the missing flow. Deliveries can continue even as the tank falls.

3 / The cushion runs out

If the delay lasts too long, less daily need can be met. The illustration signals supply pressure.

4 / The route reopens

Extra throughput clears the queue and refills the chosen buffer. Pressure can ease.

0% means this scenario's chosen buffer is empty. It does not mean all real oil tanks are empty. “Price pressure” describes an assumed direction; there is no dollar-price prediction here.

Assumptions, simple arithmetic and what is left out

Normal route capacity is assumed to be 20 vessel-equivalents a day; one vessel-equivalent carries an assumed 0.2 million barrels. The queue starts at zero. Daily need equals normal arrivals. Stocks cover the gap while capacity is restricted, then spare capacity refills stock after reopening. End-of-disruption results below the animation are different from the current playback time.

Queue = max(0, arrivals − capacity) × duration. Chosen buffer = arrivals × buffer days. Unbuffered delayed cargo = max(0, queue − buffer) × assumed cargo per vessel. Clearance time = queue ÷ (20 − arrivals), with arrivals unchanged.

No live AIS, measured tank levels, tanker classes, rerouting, refinery outages or retail-price response are estimated. Refining and delivery lags are compressed. Delay is not necessarily permanent supply loss. No animation value enters the statistical forecasts or prediction ranges.

HYPOTHETICAL CONDITIONAL LEVEL

The assumptions behind this scenario
ΔP / P ≈ (demand shock − supply shock) / elasticity

Supply and demand changes are percentages of a common global quantity baseline. The positive denominator combines supply and absolute demand elasticities. This is a local linear approximation; large shocks, substitution, inventories and regional constraints can invalidate it. The 0.10–0.50 range is an assumption, not a confidence interval.

PART 02 / CHECK THE EVIDENCE

What the data supports, where models help and where uncertainty remains.

03 / QUESTION & EVIDENCE

What can the evidence support?

The original question linked fear, trading and shipping to oil prices. The rebuilt test asks something narrower: can a forecast make smaller mistakes than keeping today's price?

Short-term ranges can catch more prices when widened. Historical relationships and scenarios do not establish what caused a price move.

04 / MODELS & PRICE

Do the models make fewer mistakes?

Compare every method on the same dates. Smaller dollar mistakes are better; a tiny historical advantage may still be luck.

All candidates, exact errors and uncertainty checks

Six new candidates target typical changes, resist large one-off moves or pull estimates toward no change. Every candidate uses the exact original forecast dates and only matured training targets. The new design was chosen after earlier results were seen; 2026 is not a fresh test. Bootstrap ranges and multiple-comparison adjustments are exploratory.

Full extension evidence · Every new forecast
Original five-model study, archived projections and trading-band checks

Expanding training window · first 252 aligned observations for warm-up · forecasts every fifth observation · fixed model settings · historical revisions remain a limitation.

Intervals need checking.

The nominal 90% intervals use the rolling 90th percentile of absolute errors from already matured forecasts, with at least 30 past errors. Observed coverage below 90% exposes instability. Overlapping horizons reduce effective sample size.

Bollinger Bands do not promise reversal.

The signals are delayed one observation. Spot unit PnL excludes financing, futures rolls and market execution; it is not an investable return series.

Latest statistical projections

05 / RELIABILITY

How much should we trust the range?

A forecast range is a safety margin around the price estimate. A useful range should catch the price often, without becoming so wide that it says very little.

Each dot represents one dated 2026 forecast. Green means the actual price landed inside its range; orange means it fell outside. These are observed-price steps, not calendar days. The target is about nine in ten; it is not a guarantee.

Inspect the methods, full comparisons and research ranges

Does it beat simply making every interval wider?

The 90% interval score equals width plus 20 times any distance outside the interval. It penalizes wide ranges and severe misses together. Higher coverage with a worse score is a tradeoff, not an unqualified improvement.

How uncertain is the improvement?

Paired 2,000-draw circular block bootstrap on 2026 origins. Negative differences favor the candidate. Ranges crossing zero do not establish a clear score improvement. Intervals overlap in time and these ranges are exploratory and unadjusted.

Latest research ranges

Legacy origin 3 November 2026. Point predictions are unchanged. New interval candidates are labeled research alternatives; they do not replace the earlier forecasts or constitute a newly issued prospective test.

Methods and remaining limits

Scaled methods divide matured forecast errors by EWMA dollar volatility known at their own origins, then multiply the empirical score quantile by current volatility. Adaptive updates use only interval misses whose targets have matured. All methods require at least 30 prior errors. The nominal target is 90%; these capped empirical quantiles and delayed-feedback updates carry no guaranteed conditional coverage.

    How we checked this · methods and full results

    What was actually varied

    Training caps of 252, 504 and 756 matured rows; weekly release lags of 7, 10 and 14 calendar days; daily delays of 1 and 2 days; ridge penalties 10, 100 and 1,000; boosting leaves 3, 7 and 15; omitted risk, inventory, production, demand and Brent inputs; removal of 2020-shock training examples; weekly frequency; market phases; non-overlapping targets; and extreme-move influence.

    Daily sensitivity models share every second original origin, equivalent to every ten WTI observations. Each row is compared with a random walk on its exact dates. Changes are one at a time; small samples and interactions remain limitations.

    What remains unverified

      The 2020 extension uses 2017–2019 warm-up data already in the raw snapshots. It is a separate retrospective experiment. Legacy-origin forecasts and rules have been saved, but they do not constitute a new prospective experiment. A true forward study needs new timestamped forecast origins issued before their outcomes. No new outcomes have been scored and no monitoring service is running.
